newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - November 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - November 25.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Police and the military carry out major search operation in Colombo, on information that a group of Tamil tiger separatists were in the capital. Separatist leader Prabakaran's birthday falls this week, which the rebels call Martyr's week.
Police to begin aerial traffic surveillance to combat congestion on city roads, says Colombo police chief D.M.T.B.Dissanayake.
Colombo traffic police to start aerial surveillance and use unmarked vehicles to check errant motorists, says city police chief.
Deputy Defence Minister Anuruddha Ratwatte calls on army deserters to return and join hands to fight separatists.
Provincial councils controlled by the opposition United National party to stop co-operating in development projects approved by the central government, from 1997.
Police officer who allegedly called a Sri Lanka Telecom office regarding a suicide attack on the installation, taken in for questioning, police sources sy.
